subject: Follow-up: DPA request, SCC module path & controller/processor alignment
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@finvera.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-25T14:05:00Z
Subject: Quick follow-up and next steps from today's privacy/security call

Alex / Maya / Finvera team — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're all aligned: 

Call highlights (short):
- Finvera running on EU-hosted infra with a mix of production and staging data for initial pilot.
- Primary compliance asks: SOC 2 Type II evidence, GDPR DPA with SCC selection, and confirmation of Controller vs Processor responsibilities for the pilot data flows.
- Potential HIPAA applicability flagged for a subset of customers — you said legal will confirm.

Immediate asks you made:
1) Formal DPA request doc from Finvera (so our legal can map clauses).
2) Which SCC module Finvera prefers (standard Modules 1–4; you mentioned Module 2 + processor amendment as an option).
3) Questionnaire kickoff — you requested the vendor security questionnaire (we can supply our XLS).

What Redwood will provide:
- SOC 2 Type II report (latest) and evidence links — attaching the questionnaire + sample DPA and a short evidence map.
- Suggested SCC approach based on our standard practice for EU customers.
- A short mutual action plan with deadlines so procurement/legal can track.

Proposed next steps / timeline:
- Today (Nov 25): You send the DPA request PDF and confirm whether Finvera will act as Controller for pilot customer data.
- Nov 26: Redwood to send completed questionnaire + sample DPA (Processor amendment highlighted).
- Nov 30: Target for both legal teams to confirm SCC module selection and sign-off approach.

Attachments included for quick review: Finvera_DPA_request.pdf (placeholder you mentioned), Redwood_Security_Questionnaire_v2.xlsx, Redwood_Sample-DPA-Processor-Amendment.docx

If that matches your expectation, I'll drop a HubSpot task and loop in our legal lead (Jonas) for clause-level questions.

Thanks —
Naomi Feldman
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Finvera Legal Team <legal@finvera.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Torres <alex.torres@finvera.com>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@finvera.com>
Date: 2026-11-26T09:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up and next steps from today's privacy/security call

Hi Naomi — thanks for the summary. Attaching the official DPA request PDF and a short note on our controller/processor stance. A couple of clarifications before we proceed to module selection: 

1) Pilot scope: Finvera will act as Controller for customer telemetry and transaction metadata; Redwood will process and store hashes and derived embeddings — we currently view you as Processor for the pilot. We will confirm whether any subsets trigger HIPAA by EOD 2026-11-27.

2) SCC module: we are inclined toward Module 2 with a Processor Amendment (our procurement prefers clearer processor obligations). Can you confirm if Redwood has prior precedence signing Module 2 + processor amendment, or if Module 3 is significantly easier operationally?

3) SOC 2: we need the last SOC 2 report plus the scope statement (which systems were in-scope). Can you indicate whether hosting is fully within Redwood's control or if any third-party cloud provider access would be out-of-scope?

We'll review the questionnaire once we receive it.

Regards,
Finvera Legal
legal@finvera.com

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Finvera Legal Team <legal@finvera.com>
Cc: Alex Torres <alex.torres@finvera.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-26T13:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up and next steps from today's privacy/security call

Hi — thanks for the details, and helpful to have the controller determination upfront. Short answers inline below: 

1) Controller/Processor: Understood that Finvera will be Controller for telemetry/transaction metadata. For the pilot, Redwood will act as Processor for that dataset. If any dataset is later deemed PHI/HIPAA-relevant we'll escalate and treat as a separate onboarding stream (we do offer HIPAA addendum options).

2) SCC module: Redwood has signed Module 2 + Processor Amendment previously on a few EU customers. Operationally, Module 3 can be simpler if the customer insists on a more provider-centric model, but Module 2 + amendment aligns best with Finvera's ask for explicit processor obligations. I'll flag Jonas for clause-level question review.

3) SOC 2: Our SOC 2 Type II (2026) will be sent as an evidence link; scope includes our inference runtime, key management integrations, and logging/alerting subsystems. We use a mix of colo-managed GPU clusters and cloud-hosted control plane; I will ask security to annotate any third-party dependencies in the scope statement.

Attached: Redwood_Security_Questionnaire_v2.xlsx and Redwood_Sample-DPA-Processor-Amendment.docx (processor language highlighted).

Proposed: If Finvera is comfortable with Module 2 + Processor Amendment, let's target clause redlines by Nov 30 and execution in early Dec.

Best,
Naomi

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Finvera Legal Team <legal@finvera.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Alex Torres <alex.torres@finvera.com>
Date: 2026-11-27T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up and next steps from today's privacy/security call

Hi all — jumped in to confirm Redwood's recommended path from a legal/privacy perspective. Short guidance for Finvera procurement/legal: 

- Recommendation: Module 2 + Processor Amendment. This provides the clearest allocation for processor obligations (data return/deletion, subprocessors, audit assistance) while meeting Finvera's ask that processor responsibilities be explicit. We have precedent for this approach and a redlineable Processor Amendment (attached sample).

- SOC 2: We'll provide the 2026 Type II report and a separate scope appendix that enumerates third-party infra (colo + cloud control plane). Anything involving customer-provided credentials or direct access by a third party will be highlighted.

- HIPAA: If any dataset is later confirmed as PHI, we will treat as a separate track with a HIPAA BAA offered; that will require an expanded evidence set and implementation timeline (estimate 3–5 weeks to finalize addendum and technical controls).

Next ask from Redwood: Finvera to confirm whether procurement wants us to: (A) share our redline capability and proposed Processor Amendment first, or (B) accept your draft DPA and we provide white-labeled redlines. Either is fine — option (A) tends to speed parallel review. 

I'll be available for a quick clause review session if you want to book 30 minutes next week — proposing Tue Dec 1, 10am CET.

Jonas Weber
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
jonas.weber@redwood.com
